title: Muscles of the sole of the foot: second layer (plantar)
attribution: 3D anatomy from Z-Anatomy, built on BodyParts3D (CC BY-SA). Rendered in Blender, with surface detail added by an image model.

rows: Medial and lateral margins of the plantar surface of the calcaneus, by two heads.
Lateral margin of the tendon of flexor digitorum longus.
Straightens the oblique pull of flexor digitorum longus and helps it flex the lateral four toes.
Tendons of flexor digitorum longus in the sole.
Medial sides of the extensor expansions of the lateral four toes.
First (most medial): medial plantar nerve. Lateral three: lateral plantar nerve.
Flex the metatarsophalangeal joints and extend the interphalangeal joints of the lateral four toes.
Medial part of the posterior surface of the tibia, below the soleal line.
Bases of the distal phalanges of the lateral four toes.
Flexes the lateral four toes. Helps plantarflex the foot and support the longitudinal arches.
Lower two-thirds of the posterior surface of the fibula and the interosseous membrane.
Base of the distal phalanx of the great toe.
Flexes the great toe, which gives the final push-off in walking. Helps plantarflex the foot and support the medial longitudinal arch.
